Md Polash Ali

Statistician, researcher, and a fairly consistent believer in the fitted line.

I'm a Ph.D. student in the Department of Mathematics & Statistics at the University of South Florida (USF), working across biostatistics, public health, spatial epidemiology, and machine learning, usually somewhere between a public-health dataset and a model that refuses to converge.

7 manuscripts · 2 published TA, USF Math & Stats Tampa ← Dhaka ← Chapainawabganj

About

The short version

I grew up in Chapainawabganj, a district in Rajshahi Division known across Bangladesh for its sweet mangoes, something the people of my hometown take great pride in. I went through my secondary years at Harimohan Government High School and higher secondary at Nawabganj Government College, before moving to the University of Dhaka to study Statistics.

Today, I'm a Ph.D. student at the University of South Florida (USF), where I research statistics with a growing interest in its applications to public health. My goal is to bring statistics and public health together to contribute, in my own way, to a healthier and better society.

I'm the elder brother of twin sisters, and however far Tampa is from Chapainawabganj, I still measure a good year partly by how the mango season went back home.

Off the clock, I'm usually three episodes into a thriller or quietly relitigating whether Spider-Man's instincts beat Iron Man's engineering. I haven't fully decided.

Beyond the numbers

Marvel

Spider-Man & Iron Man

When a problem gets tangled, it's a toss-up between a web-slinger's instinct for finding the pattern in chaos and a genius engineer's habit of just building something better. Still haven't picked a side. (Every dataset has one Hulk-sized outlier, too, and a truly stubborn model earns a bit of Thor commentary about which one is actually worthy.)
